what: GEO-AMX (2026-10-24): the PR818 study's bf16 arm timed where the AMX instance runs -- the timing GEO-2 planned and could not take (its host had moved to one without AMX). The study's three models (the global head, the query-aware head and the attention baseline), GEO-2b's level-2 overlays linked with this branch's tensor unit, trained under the study's binary32 contract (14), its bf16 contract (26: the GEMMs on bfloat16 operands, the AMX instance here) and, for the attention model, the bf16 attention as well (90, BF16-ATTN), beside an A/A arm; and against PyTorch's own mixed precision (torch.autocast to bfloat16, eager and compiled, whose matmuls run oneDNN's AMX kernels here) and compiled FP32. Records only: no runtime change.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz, 4 vCPU (AVX-512F, AVX512-BF16 and -FP16, AMX-BF16 and AMX-TILE), 2 MiB of L2 a core, 260 MiB of L3 -- the host the session moved to on 2026-10-23; Linux 6.18; GCC 13.3 (the overlays' build, as the study builds them); Python 3.11 (amx_pairs.py: NumPy 2.2.6), torch 2.13.0+cu130 (CPU); OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE
bundle_reference: the bundle's own paired timing (wedge-pr818/paired-timing.log, Codex's AMD EPYC 9V74 without AMX, the bf16 GEMMs on the AVX-512F instance, which emulates the tile unit's arithmetic): 'Numerics/BF16/query_full/B4T256' FP32 over BF16 0.877 (the bf16 arm x1.14 of FP32's time) and 'Numerics/BF16/attention/B4T256' 0.960 (x1.04)
